LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.3: Guided Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we enhance handwriting in Chinese?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write simple sentences in various contexts using clear and legible handwriting
2. value the role of legible handwriting in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING
Subject: MANDARIN · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing helps you succeed in MANDARIN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Write simple sentences in various contexts using clear and legible handwriting

What this means
In this part you learn to write simple sentences in various contexts using clear and legible handwriting. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write simple sentences in various contexts using clear and legible handwriting.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write simple sentences in various contexts using clear and legible handwriting. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Value the role of legible handwriting in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to value the role of legible handwriting in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the role of legible handwriting in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the role of legible handwriting in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: write simple sentences in various contexts using clear and legible handwriting)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing to a partner. (skill: value the role of legible handwriting in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: write simple sentences in various contexts using clear and legible handwriting.
3. Practise this skill: value the role of legible handwriting in communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Guided Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we enhance handwriting in Chinese?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: write simple sentences in various contexts using clear and legible handwriting.
5. Be able to: value the role of legible handwriting in communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
